glossary.def: National Medical Commission. India's regulator for doctors and medical education.
Registered Medical Practitioner. A doctor whose name is in the National Register or a State Medical Register.
State Medical Register and National Medical Register. The doctor's registration number comes from one of these.
State Medical Council. It takes disciplinary action against a doctor under the guidelines.
Ethics and Medical Registration Board of NMC. The appeals body, and the issuer of the notice.
The “Guidelines on Ethical Advertising and Public Communication by hospitals/medical institutions and Registered Medical Practitioners” dated 06/10/2026.

Any communication, in any medium, that directly or indirectly promotes a doctor's or hospital's services, reputation or skills. Digital, social, sponsored, influencer, search and AI content count if promotional.

Where an advertisement appears: print, TV, radio, social, websites, blogs, WhatsApp and other messaging, podcasts, influencers, digital campaigns, AI promotion, promotional articles and online healthcare platforms.
A place that provides diagnosis, treatment or care, including clinics covered by the Clinical Establishments Act 2010 or a State Act.
A patient's statement praising a doctor or clinic. Not allowed for promotion, and consent does not change that.
A person, such as a celebrity, influencer, patient or staff member, recommending a doctor, clinic or product.
Photos or videos that show a patient's appearance or condition before and after treatment. Not allowed, except in a narrow scientific or educational case.
Directly or indirectly seeking patients, for example through inducements, offers or heavy promotion.
A benefit such as a discount, coupon, gift, cashback or free procedure that pushes people to take treatment.
A claim that a doctor or clinic is better than others: best, No.1, leading, top, unmatched.
Can be proved by an independent source using a clear, published method. A self-made claim is not verifiable.
Consent from a patient whose identity is hidden in the published material. It is relevant only for the narrow scientific or educational exception.
A visible label stating that content was generated by AI.
A self-learning automated process or machine built to do tasks that usually need a human brain.
Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, with Rules made in 2025. India's data-protection law.
A written notice asking a doctor to explain an alleged violation before any penalty.
Google Business Profile. The listing that appears on Google Search and Maps.
Dynamic keyword insertion. A Google Ads feature that inserts the searcher's keyword into the ad text automatically.
Code on a web page that tells search engines about its content, such as ratings or business details.
The page a person arrives on after clicking an ad.
A payment for each enquiry or contact delivered. The document restricts such fees where tied to patient referral or procurement.
A label used in this guide for advice that is ours and not stated in the NMC document.

faq.q: Do we have to delete all our educational blogs?
faq.a: No. Information given to the public without a promotional purpose is exempt. Keep educational posts and fix only what is promotional: claims, results, offers, heavy sales calls to action. Add the doctor byline.

faq.q: The patient gave written consent. Can we keep the testimonial or before-and-after?
faq.a: No. The document says consent does not make a prohibited practice permissible.

faq.q: Can we still say the clinic has a particular laser or machine?
faq.a: Yes, as a fact. Do not say it is the most advanced, accurate or guaranteed to work.
Yes. Charges can be shown if they are factual, transparent and not misleading. Do not frame them as an offer or discount.

faq.q: What do we need to show about the doctor?
faq.a: Name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR registration number, on electronic posts. A clinic must name its doctors in the same way.

faq.q: Can we use “best”, “top” or “leading” if the client has an award?
faq.a: Only if the claim is objectively verifiable with an independent, transparent methodology. Awards must be verifiable and their body, date and conditions disclosed where needed. Leadership signs off.

faq.q: Can we run influencer or celebrity campaigns?
faq.a: No for promotion. The document bars promotion by celebrities, influencers, patients and employees, and bars using a third party to do indirectly what is prohibited.

faq.q: Can we ask patients for Google reviews?
faq.a: We do not. Soliciting reviews is barred, and a doctor must not request or share reviews for promotion on social media. Whether a neutral, passive link is allowed is an open question.

faq.q: Can we use AI to make images, videos or copy?
faq.a: Be very careful. AI promotional campaigns are prohibited, compliant AI promotional content needs a source mark, and AI must not create synthetic patients, voices, endorsements or outcomes.

faq.q: Who gets penalised, the doctor or us?
faq.a: The penalties described are against the doctor (by the State Medical Council) or the clinic (under State law). Using an agency does not remove the doctor's responsibility. Our risk is losing clients and contractual disputes.

First violation: warning and ethics training. Second: censure and monetary penalty. Third: suspension of registration for 3–6 months. Serious violations: 6–12 months. Repeated: removal for 1–3 years. These “may be contemplated” by the State Medical Council.

faq.q: Can the doctor appear on the website or in ads with a photo?
faq.a: It depends. A photo is not allowed where it is self-advertisement or promotional publicity.

faq.q: Can we offer a festival discount or giveaway?
faq.a: No. Discounts, limited-period offers, contests, coupons, gifts, cashbacks and free procedures are listed inducements.

faq.q: What if a client insists on something the guide says not to do?
faq.a: Do not publish it. Escalate to your department lead and Leadership. The client is responsible for what they authorise, but we do not publish prohibited content.
Possibly. NMC may issue clarifications, advisories and SOPs. Leadership checks monthly and updates the guide.
